intel_reference: Intel SDM rev 092, Vol. 2A, BSF, 3-107/3-108 (PDF pp. 224-225)
intel_fact: Zero source leaves the destination unmodified. ZF reports a zero source; PF is parity of the source; CF/OF/SF/AF are cleared. Footnotes retain older-processor exceptions.
amd_reference: AMD APM Vol. 3 rev 3.37, BSF, p. 123
amd_fact: Zero source leaves the destination unchanged. ZF reports a zero source; OF/SF/AF/PF/CF are undefined.
portable_rule: A cross-vendor lowering may depend on ZF. It must not depend on PF/CF/OF/SF/AF after BSF. If old Intel processors are in scope, do not infer full-width zero-source destination preservation from the current Intel rule.

intel_reference: Intel SDM rev 092, Vol. 2B, SYSCALL, 4-698..4-700 (PDF pp. 705-707)
intel_fact: SYSCALL is recognized only in 64-bit mode; protected, real, virtual-8086, and compatibility modes raise #UD. The non-FRED path enters through IA32_LSTAR.
amd_reference: AMD APM combined Vols. 1-5 rev 4.09, Vol. 1 section 3.7.7.1 and Vol. 2 section 6.1.1
amd_fact: AMD documents SYSCALL/SYSRET for protected mode as well as long mode. STAR contains a 32-bit SYSCALL target EIP; LSTAR and CSTAR provide 64-bit-mode and compatibility-mode targets in long mode.
portable_rule: Do not infer a vendor-neutral 32-bit/compatibility SYSCALL contract. The current Idriç Linux x86-64 path may use SYSCALL because it deliberately targets 64-bit mode and an OS ABI, not because the mnemonic is mode-portable.

intel_reference: Intel SDM rev 092, Vol. 2B, SYSRET, 4-708..4-710 (PDF pp. 715-717)
intel_fact: SYSRET executes from 64-bit mode; its non-REX.W form can return to compatibility mode, but SYSRET is not recognized in protected mode.
amd_reference: AMD APM combined Vols. 1-5 rev 4.09, Vol. 1 section 3.7.7.1 and Vol. 2 section 6.1.1
amd_fact: AMD documents SYSCALL/SYSRET as usable in protected mode and documents 32-bit return selectors in STAR.
portable_rule: Do not model SYSRET as having one vendor-neutral mode-availability rule. Keep protected-mode use vendor-specific; the 64-bit backend does not need SYSRET today.
